name: Cate Collins
title: Director of Tour Operations & Lead Scientist
company: Classic Canadian Tours / Gold Star Canadian Tours
headline: Good to meet you,
Cate
lede: You run wildlife trips in places with weather, permits and no infrastructure — polar bears, grizzlies, the Yukon in winter. We do the same thing at altitude. You asked Brian about wildlife, and about what works for a group traveling in its seventies. This page is the short answer to both.

facts.label: Countries we operate in: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China
Years running our own crews in the region
The altitude band our programs work in, Bhutan valleys to Ladakh passes
Guides and logistics, never subcontracted

angle.eyebrow: — Where a Canadian wildlife operator and a Himalayan one actually meet
angle.heading: You asked about wildlife. We have two answers, and they sit at opposite ends of the effort scale.
angle.body: Ladakh in winter is the one place on earth where snow leopard sightings are a realistic itinerary rather than a lottery ticket — but it is a hard, cold trip, and it is not the one for most of your guests. Bhutan is. Black-necked cranes winter at Khotokha from late October to mid-February, and the watching is done from level ground, a short walk from a warm room, with monasteries and village life in the same day. One species is an expedition. The other is a wildlife trip an eighty-year-old can do well.

cards.eyebrow: The one we do not put on the website
cards.title: We are building in Bhutan, not just operating there
cards.body: Brian and Kinley Tshering are partners in a lodge under construction at Khotokha — 8,500 ft, in Wangdue Phodrang — where the cranes winter. Brian moves his family to Thimphu this fall. For an operator who sells all-inclusive, it means the beds on a Bhutan wildlife itinerary are ours rather than brokered. Brian will tell you where it stands in person; it is not on our website, and it is not open yet.
cards.note: Will authorized naming Khotokha on THIS page, 15 Sep, overriding the standing teaser-only rule. THE PROPERTY IS NOT NAMED — do not add a name, key count, opening date or terms. Everything stated here comes from Brian's 2 Sep note: partners, location, under construction, the Thimphu move. Note the page is publicly reachable and /m/cate-collins is guessable.

cards.title: Referral, both directions
cards.body: A guest who has done Churchill and the Yukon in the same year is running out of Canadian firsts. We would happily be the place you send them next, and send ours to you when they ask about polar bears.

cards.title: Science-led programming
cards.body: You carry a Lead Scientist on staff, which most operators do not. Both landscapes have live conservation work attached — crane monitoring and habitat protection in Bhutan, snow leopard and glaciology research in high Ladakh — which a scientifically framed itinerary can sit alongside rather than simply drive past.
cards.note: Confirm what wildlife programming Adventure Access actually runs, in BOTH Bhutan and Ladakh, before any of this is claimed as product. The page is written as 'this is what is there and we build to profile', not 'we have a crane departure' — keep it that way unless Brian says otherwise.

specifics.title: Bhutan is the wildlife trip that works for your demographic.
specifics.body: The black-necked cranes are at Khotokha through the winter, and the watching is roadside and valley-floor rather than a scramble. Days pair easily with dzongs, monasteries and village visits, which is the mix you described. The one number worth knowing up front is the altitude: Khotokha sits at 8,500 ft, so the itinerary has to be built to arrive there gently rather than on day two.

specifics.title: We are building where the cranes winter.
specifics.body: That is the part most operators cannot offer. On a wildlife itinerary built around a narrow season, the accommodation is usually the first thing to fail — and at Khotokha it will be ours. Ask Brian in the room; the build is not something we put on the web.

specifics.title: The season is the mirror image of yours.
specifics.body: Snow leopard tracking is a February and March activity, when Ladakh is at its coldest and the cats come down from higher altitudes. The Bhutan crane window runs late October to mid-February. Both sit squarely in your Canadian shoulder season.

specifics.title: Pace is a build decision, not a compromise.
specifics.body: We construct to a client profile rather than selling fixed departures, so an itinerary for travelers in their seventies and eighties is a different build, not a shortened version of a younger one — shorter driving days, lower sleeping altitudes, cultural depth carrying the days that activity would otherwise carry.

specifics.title: Permits are the real barrier, not the terrain.
specifics.body: Ladakh's inner-line areas need permits that change without notice, and Bhutan runs on the Sustainable Development Fee and a licensed-operator system. It is the same class of problem as operating in the Yukon, and it is the part we already solve.

specifics.title: No infrastructure means the operator is the product.
specifics.body: You know this already. There is no supplier chain to fall back on in Zanskar in winter; the trip is whoever is standing there.

closing.heading: Nothing to sell you today.
closing.body: Eleanor's read was that our specialties are too different for a straightforward commercial fit. Your note to Brian moved that — wildlife, an older and slower group, a mix of activity and culture, is a brief we can actually build to, and Bhutan is where we are putting our own money. So this stays a conversation between two people who operate in hard places, with something concrete on the table.

specificsNote: RESOLVED 15 Sep: altitude band widened to 4,000–17,700 ft; Khotokha named at Will's direction; the crane content is attributed to Khotokha only, with no other valley named and no bird counts; THE PROPERTY IS DELIBERATELY UNNAMED. STILL OPEN: confirm what wildlife programming Adventure Access actually runs, in Bhutan and Ladakh both — the page is written as 'this is what is there and we build to profile', not 'we have a crane departure'. Also: Cate said the mountain biking 'looks incredible' personally. Worth raising in the room; deliberately not on the page, because it is not what she would buy for her groups.

name: Andrea Vinyard
title: Owner & Travel Advisor
headline: Good to meet you,
Andrea
lede: Seven continents and nearly a hundred countries — you have been further than most of the people selling this region. So this is not a page about the Himalaya being wonderful. It is about the one part of the map where your hotel program runs out of rooms, and what we can do about it.

facts.label: Countries we operate: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China
Years on the ground with our own staff
A Himalayan lodge of our own — ask me in the room
Resellers between you and the people running the trip

angle.heading: Find a cruise, find a hotel, find a tour. The Himalaya is the place where all three come back thin.
angle.body: Going Places can put a client almost anywhere in the world through Cruise Planners and Signature — and that works everywhere there is chain inventory and a supplier with a rate sheet. Bhutan, Ladakh, Nepal and the Tibetan plateau are the exception. The properties worth staying in are small, family-run and not in anyone's booking engine, and the trip around them cannot be assembled from a screen. That is the whole of what we do, and we would rather extend what you already sell than ask you to replace it.

cards.eyebrow: For the suppliers you already use
cards.title: We sit underneath, not in front
cards.body: You are not being asked to drop anyone. We are the ground layer — permits, licensed guides, vehicles, rooms — so a Himalayan segment becomes something your existing operators and your own custom land tours can actually carry.

cards.eyebrow: For your land and stay business
cards.title: Places to stay that are not on any engine
cards.body: Village houses, monastery guesthouses, a handful of genuinely good small hotels, and one property of our own. It widens where you can place a client without widening the list of people you have to manage.

specifics.title: Permits, in plain terms.
specifics.body: Ladakh's inner-line permits change without notice, Bhutan runs on the Sustainable Development Fee and a licensed-operator rule, Nepal has its restricted areas. Different regimes, none alike, all of them moving. They are ours to hold and manage, not yours to track.

specifics.title: A place of our own — and it is not on the internet.
specifics.body: Alongside the ground operation we are building a small lodge of our own in the Himalaya. Nothing about it is public yet, so there is nothing to look up and nothing to send you. It is the part of this worth two minutes across the table, because it changes what a Going Places client can be offered in a region where the answer today is usually a three-star in a capital city.

specifics.title: One contact, four countries.
specifics.body: A client who wants Nepal and Bhutan in one trip is two suppliers, two contracts and a handoff at the border. With us it is one itinerary, one person answering the phone, and your client relationship untouched.

closing.heading: You keep the client. We keep the ground.
closing.body: The fastest way to judge us is not a brochure — it is one real client and one real set of dates. Send a live brief and you will know more about us in a week than any deck would tell you.

specificsNote: Teaser rule holds: no name, village, key count, timeline or terms for the lodge anywhere on this page. Confirm with Brian how much he wants said in the room.

name: Monica Price
title: Owner / Director of International Operations
headline: Good to meet you,
Monica
lede: Fifty years of supported cycling across Europe, Latin America and Africa — and nothing yet on the Asian side of the map. This page is the short version of what we could put there, and the one question we want to ask you in person.

facts.label: Years ExperiencePlus! has been running bicycle tours
Asian itineraries currently on your map
Years across the Himalaya with our own crews — 5+ of them in Ladakh
The riding window, once the passes clear

angle.eyebrow: — The question we actually want to ask you
angle.heading: Do your riders want tarmac, or do they want dirt?
angle.body: It changes the whole proposition, and we would rather ask than guess. Your catalog reads as road touring; the Ladakh product we run today is shuttle-supported mountain biking. Both are buildable. They are not the same trip.

cards.title: The high-pass road ride
cards.body: Sealed road, support vehicle, village-scale lodging — structurally the closest thing to what you already sell. What changes is the floor as much as the ceiling: the valleys sit above 11,000 feet and the road passes run 17,500 and up — Taglang La 17,480, Khardung La 17,582, Chang La 17,590. Ladakh also holds the highest paved road on earth, Umling La at 19,024 feet, in permit-controlled border country. There is no warm-up week at sea level to build into the front of an itinerary.
cards.note: Confirm before the meeting: do we run paved/supported touring, or MTB only? And is Umling La operationally reachable for a group — permits, distance from Leh, road state?

cards.title: Zanskar, shuttle-supported
cards.body: The program we run now: caravan routes and yak trails between 11,500 and 17,700 feet, laps served by our own shuttle crew, heritage lodging at each end. This one exists and has run.

specifics.title: Altitude is handled before the bikes come out.
specifics.body: Ladakh starts at 11,500 feet. The tour opens with two soft days at Nimmu House, a heritage home in the orchards where the Indus and Zanskar meet — short walks, no riding.

specifics.title: The descents are repeatable, not one-shot.
specifics.body: Below Khar Kongma, the royal palace at Zangla, a short cliffy descent becomes shuttle laps. Higher up, the drop from Kyupa La at 14,400 feet starts on rock and scree and mellows into singletrack.

specifics.title: The season is late April to early October.
specifics.body: Once the passes clear and the ground is firm. Outside it the valleys are shut — worth knowing before a June-to-September assumption goes into print.

closing.heading: One region you are not in, run by people who live there.
closing.body: If the answer to the tarmac question is tarmac, we have work to do before we can promise it. If it is dirt, the trip already exists and has run.

specificsNote: CORRECTED 15 Sep at Will's direction. (1) The 20+ years is REGIONAL — Bhutan, India, Nepal, China, as adventure-access.com/about states — NOT 20 years in Ladakh. Will gave the Ladakh figure on 15 Sep: OVER 5 YEARS. The tile now carries both, regional first — 20+ across the Himalaya, 5+ of them in Ladakh — because a bare '5' sitting under ExperiencePlus!'s '50' invites the wrong comparison. Do not re-attach the 20+ to Ladakh alone on any page. (2) The old paved-option line read 'moved to 13,100 feet', which is below every road pass in Ladakh and below Leh's own valley floor. Replaced with the real band: valleys above 11,000 ft, road passes 17,500+. Pass elevations are the GPS-measured figures, not the inflated ones on the Khardung La signboard (which claims 18,379 ft).

name: Patricia Dubé
title: Agency Owner
headline: Good to meet you,
Patricia
lede: You build high-value travel for professionals, entrepreneurs and private groups — and the Himalaya is not on your program yet. This page is the short version of what we could put there.

facts.label: Countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China
Years living and operating across the region, with our own crews
Programs run by our own staff, not brokered
The default here, never a surcharge

angle.eyebrow: — Why this conversation is worth twelve minutes
angle.heading: A professional-development trip to the Himalaya is not a holiday in disguise.
angle.body: Continuing-education travel and corporate personas are your specialty, and that is exactly the shape the Himalaya serves best: a small group, a shared purpose, and a place that makes people pay attention. We do not sell fixed departures — we build the program around the group you bring us.

cards.title: Programs built, not catalogued
cards.body: Length, pace, comfort level and route get rebuilt around your group. Our itineraries are starting points, nothing more.
cards.note: VERIFIED 15 Sep: Odyssée Formations is a named line of the business, professional-development travel for professionals and entrepreneurs. Aventures and Mieux-être are separate lines, so she buys more than one shape.

cards.title: The access, not the destination
cards.body: Ladakh's inner-line permits change without notice, Bhutan runs on its Sustainable Development Fee and a licensed-operator system, Nepal has its restricted areas. Different regimes, none of them alike, all of them ours to carry.

specifics.title: Working in French, said plainly.
specifics.body: Our crews work in English on the ground. For a Québec group the question of French-speaking accompaniment is a real one, and we would rather put it on the table than work around it.

specifics.title: Bhutan is the one a group says yes to.
specifics.body: A country that meters its own tourism, runs on a licensed-operator system and the Sustainable Development Fee, and has a considered answer for why anyone should come. Days are valley floor and cultural rather than athletic — dzongs, monasteries, villages, a walk that ends at a good bed. For a group with a shared purpose it is the easiest Himalayan country to sell and the hardest to arrange, which is the half we carry.

specifics.title: One supplier, four countries.
specifics.body: A group that wants Nepal and Bhutan in one trip means two suppliers and a hand-off today. With us it is one itinerary and one person answering for it.

specificsNote: REWRITTEN FROM FRENCH TO ENGLISH 15 Sep at Will's direction — the page is no longer in French, and Patricia can translate it herself if she wants to. The French-on-the-ground card stays: she is a francophone Quebec agency and the question is real, so the page raises it rather than ducking it. 15 Sep: the Amdo/Kham eastern-Tibet specific was replaced with a Bhutan card at Will's direction — Bhutan and Ladakh are the stronger ground for a group page than a Tibet-permit workaround. VERIFIED 15 Sep from odysseeagence.com: Patricia Dubé founded the agency and one of its four lines is Odyssée Formations, trips built to combine discovery with skill development, sold to professionals and entrepreneurs (their own figure: 300+ professionals served). The other three lines are Aventures, Mieux-être and Signature, so professional development is her strongest line rather than her only one. Their destination list — Argentina, Costa Rica, Mexico, Norway, Portugal, Japan, Vietnam, Morocco, Tanzania, Galapagos, French Polynesia — carries no Himalaya, so not on your program yet holds. 15 Sep, Will: corporate groups reworded to corporate personas.

closing.heading: The group is the product, not the departure.
closing.body: The fastest way to judge us is a live brief: one real group, one real set of dates, and see what comes back.

name: Curtis Fox
title: Managing Partner
headline: Good to meet you,
Curtis
lede: You sell Asia, and you sell India. What your catalog does not appear to reach is the Himalaya — which is the one part of the subcontinent where private access is worth paying for, and the one part you cannot buy off a shelf.

facts.label: Countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China
Years operating there with our own people
Every program built for one party, not a departure
Resellers between you and the ground

angle.eyebrow: — Why this conversation is worth twelve minutes
angle.heading: Discerning explorers is the phrase on your site. The Himalaya is where that phrase gets tested.
angle.body: Private travel in Europe means a better hotel and a good driver. Private travel in Ladakh or Bhutan means permits nobody else can get, a crew who live there, and an itinerary that can be rebuilt at forty-eight hours' notice because the pass closed. That is a harder product to source and a much easier one to sell.

cards.title: Custom private journeys
cards.body: Already your core product. Ours too — we would rather rebuild an itinerary than sell you a fixed departure that half fits.

cards.title: Your hosted founder's trip
cards.body: A founder-hosted Himalayan departure is a natural fit for this region, and the kind of trip that is remembered rather than repeated.
cards.note: Ask what the hosted founder's trip actually is before pitching into it.

specifics.title: Four permit regimes, none of them alike.
specifics.body: Tibet travel permits, Ladakh inner-line, Bhutan's Sustainable Development Fee, Nepal's restricted areas. We hold the licenses and the relationships; you hold the client.

specifics.title: Expedition-grade without the expedition.
specifics.body: You already sell cruises and expeditions. The plateau delivers the same remoteness with a bed at the end of the day and no ship's schedule.

specifics.title: Small by design.
specifics.body: We are a small team on purpose — you deal with the people who actually run the trip, which is the only way a private program stays private.

closing.heading: The access is the product.
closing.body: The fastest way to judge us is a live brief: one real client, one real set of dates, and see what comes back.

name: Tilghman Whitacre
title: Travel Advisor
headline: Good to meet you,
Tilghman
lede: Fora advisors already sell Bhutan, Nepal, India and China. So the useful conversation is not whether the region sells — it is what an advisor needs from a ground operator in order to sell it without fear.

facts.label: Of the destinations Fora lists are our home ground
Years operating there with our own crews
What it takes us to rebuild an itinerary on the ground
Person you talk to, who also runs the trip

angle.eyebrow: — What an advisor actually needs from a Himalayan operator
angle.heading: The reason advisors avoid the Himalaya is not demand. It is that nobody wants to be the reason the plan falls apart.
angle.body: An advisor is selling their own judgment. That makes an unfamiliar region a reputational risk long before it is a commercial one, and it is why the same clients get sold Japan a second time instead of Bhutan a first. What we can offer is the thing that removes that risk: the operator on the other end of the email is the operator on the mountain.

cards.title: One advisor, a network behind them
cards.body: If this works for your clients, it works for the advisors who ask you what you used. We would rather earn that slowly and properly than be listed somewhere.
cards.note: Ask how a supplier actually works with Fora — centrally, or advisor by advisor?

cards.title: Something you can forward
cards.body: A quick-quote turnaround, clear commission terms, and one page an advisor can send a client without rewriting it. Tell us what shape that needs to take.

specifics.title: Quotes come back with the permits already checked.
specifics.body: Not a price with an asterisk. If an inner-line area is closed or an SDF change lands, it is in the quote before you see it.

specifics.title: International, wellness, luxury, adventure — all four at once.
specifics.body: Those are the four things your own page asks clients to come to you about. A Himalayan trip is the rare itinerary that is all four in a single booking: hard days earned on the trail, somewhere quiet and well-run to recover, and a place most of your clients have never been offered.

specifics.title: A place of our own — and it is not on the internet.
specifics.body: A small lodge of our own in the Himalaya. Nothing public, no listing, no booking engine, no way for a client to find it without you. For an advisor who sells the part where the tent ends and the pampering begins, it is worth two minutes across the table.

specificsNote: UPDATED 15 Sep at Will's direction. (1) The bold angle heading no longer turns on a failed permit — it is now that nobody wants to be the reason the plan falls apart. (2) The Amdo/Kham 'no Tibet permit' specific is REMOVED and replaced with the lodge, as a TEASER ONLY: no name, no village, no district, no key count, no timeline, no terms. The standing teaser rule holds on this page — Khotokha is named on Cate Collins' page alone. (3) specifics[1] now carries the four ASK ME ABOUT categories read verbatim off foratravel.com/advisor/tilghman-whitacre on 15 Sep — International Travel, Wellness Travel, Luxury Travel, Adventure Travel — replacing the unverified 'group travel and celebrations are two of the categories Fora lists' claim. Her own profile is the source for the adventure-then-indulge framing too: she describes herself as a tent-sleeping mountain lover who specialises in exclusive resorts and boutique hideaways for afterwards. STILL UNVERIFIED: the lede's claim that Fora advisors already sell Bhutan, Nepal, India and China came from the same research sheet that had Andrea Vinyard as a different company. STILL OPEN: how a supplier actually works with Fora — centrally, or advisor by advisor?

closing.heading: Sell your judgment. We will stand behind it.
closing.body: Start with one client and one brief. If we are wrong for Fora you will know inside a week, and so will we.

name: Nahum Avila
title: Travel Advisor
headline: Good to meet you,
Nahum
lede: You already send clients to Asia — Thailand, Japan, Vietnam. The Himalaya is the step above: the trip for the client who has done all three and is asking what comes next.

facts.label: Countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China
Years on the ground there, with our own crews
Asian destinations on your program today
Every program rebuilt around the client

angle.eyebrow: — Why this conversation is worth twelve minutes
angle.heading: The client coming home from Thailand is rarely looking for another beach.
angle.body: Your Asia program is solid and mainstream. The Himalaya does not replace it — it gives it somewhere to go next. It is the trip you sell once to the right client, and that they talk about for ten years.

cards.title: One first product, not a catalogue
cards.body: There is no need to build a region. One good itinerary — Nepal or Bhutan — is enough to find out whether your clients follow you there.
cards.note: VERIFIED 15 Sep from voyagespleinsoleil.ca/destinations: their Asia page names Thailand, Japan and Vietnam, not Indonesia. The lede is corrected. Their wording is Thailand, Japan, Vietnam et ailleurs, so three is the named count rather than a ceiling.

cards.title: And the paperwork behind it
cards.body: Whichever one you start with, the entry rules are ours to hold — Bhutan's Sustainable Development Fee and licensed-operator rule, Nepal's restricted areas, and Ladakh's inner-line permits, which change without notice and are the reason most of that region never reaches a brochure. We track them and build around them. None of it lands on your desk.

specifics.title: Working in French, said plainly.
specifics.body: Our crews work in English on the ground. For a Québec clientele that is a real question, and we would rather meet it head-on than work around it.

specifics.title: Groups and escorted departures.
specifics.body: You already run groups. A private Himalayan departure sells like one, with ground operations that do not disappear the moment the group lands.

specifics.title: The season decides everything.
specifics.body: The windows are short and not negotiable — the passes open and close. Worth knowing before dates go into a brochure.

specificsNote: REWRITTEN FROM FRENCH TO ENGLISH 15 Sep at Will's direction — the page is no longer in French, and Nahum can translate it himself if he wants to. The French-on-the-ground card stays: Voyage Plein Soleil is a francophone Quebec agency and the question is real. VERIFIED 15 Sep: their own destinations page names Thailand, Japan and Vietnam. Indonesia was wrong and is out. One open item: the row now reads Voyages Plein Soleil (plural), matching their own site and every directory listing (Will, 15 Sep). The HubSpot record still says Voyage; worth matching before Wednesday.

closing.heading: One itinerary is a small bet.
closing.body: Pick a single trip — Nepal or Bhutan — put it in front of your best Asia clients and see who bites. We build it and run it; the client stays yours.

name: Scott Abbott
title: Managing Director
headline: Good to meet you,
Scott
lede: You already run Bhutan, Nepal, Tibet and India. We are not here to sell you a destination you have been programming for years — we are here to ask which parts of it are hardest to operate, because those are the parts we are for.

facts.label: Countries, all of them already on your map
Years living and operating in them
Run by our own people, never farmed out
Interest in competing with your itineraries

angle.eyebrow: — The honest version of why we asked for twelve minutes
angle.heading: The wrong question is whether you would sell what we have. The right one is what operational gaps we could fill.
angle.body: A company with your catalog does not need a Bhutan supplier; you have one. What you may have is a set of places your itineraries stop short of, or a region where the ground handling has been merely adequate for a long time. That is a more interesting conversation than a capability deck, and a shorter one.

cards.eyebrow: Where we think the gap is
cards.title: Ladakh and Zanskar
cards.body: Scheduled far less often than Bhutan or the Everest region, harder to operate, and some of our deepest ground. High-altitude trekking and riding out of Leh with Ladakhi guides.

cards.eyebrow: And one that is not on the internet
cards.title: The one nobody knows
cards.body: Alongside the ground operation we are building a small lodge of our own in the Himalaya. Nothing about it is public — no listing, no booking engine, nothing to look up and nothing to send you. For a company that has been placing clients in this region for years, it is the one bed you cannot already book. Two minutes across the table with Brian is the whole of it.

specifics.title: Our guides are from the valleys they guide in.
specifics.body: Ladakhi, Nepali, Bhutanese and eastern Tibetan staff working on home ground — including Stanzin Padma, leading treks in a place where that was not a job women did.

specifics.title: Mountain biking as a discipline, not an add-on.
specifics.body: Zanskar riding between 11,500 and 17,700 feet on caravan routes and yak trails, with our own shuttle crew. If it is not in your catalog, it is because almost nobody can run it.

specifics.title: Licensed where it matters.
specifics.body: Tibet permits, Ladakh inner-line, Bhutan SDF, Nepal restricted areas. Not a brokered relationship — ours.

closing.heading: Tell us where it hurts.
closing.body: Twelve minutes is enough to name one operational problem. If we can solve it, that is a better start than a proposal neither of us asked for.

name: Breanne Kiefner
title: Founder
headline: Good to meet you,
Breanne
lede: Trekking, cultural immersion, wellness, custom and self-guided — of everyone we are meeting this week, your product list overlaps ours most closely. Which makes this the easiest conversation to have and the easiest one to waste on generalities.

facts.label: Countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China
Years running our own crews there
Local guides, on their own home ground
The default, not an upgrade

angle.eyebrow: — The specific thing we would like to talk about
angle.heading: Self-guided in the Himalaya is the hardest thing on your list, and the one that most needs a local operator.
angle.body: Self-guided works in Europe because the infrastructure carries the traveler. In Nepal or Ladakh there is no infrastructure to carry anyone: permits, transfers, closed valleys, altitude. Self-guided there does not mean unsupported — it means invisibly supported, which is a ground operator's job rather than a route description.

cards.title: Trekking and cultural immersion
cards.body: Your two strongest categories and our two deepest. Guides from the valleys they guide in, and routes that are not the queue.

cards.title: Wellness that is not a spa
cards.body: Altitude, silence, walking and monastery towns do something a retreat cannot. Bhutan in particular priced its tourism for value over volume, which is why it still feels that way.

specifics.title: Like-hearted travel needs small groups, and small groups need ground.
specifics.body: Your phrase, and it is the right one. Groups of that size only work when the operator can absorb a change without renegotiating with a consolidator.

specifics.title: acclimatization built in, not bolted on.
specifics.body: Ladakh starts at 11,500 feet. Our programs open with soft days at low activity because pretending altitude is not there is the most common way these trips fail.

specifics.title: Four countries, one itinerary.
specifics.body: Nepal and Bhutan in one trip is currently two suppliers and a handoff. With us it is one operator and one set of permits.

closing.heading: The overlap is obvious. The useful part is what you cannot currently run.
closing.body: If there is a trip you have wanted to offer and shelved because the ground was not there, that is the twelve minutes well spent.

name: Meagan Coates
title: Director of Product
headline: Good to meet you,
Meagan
lede: Cycling and hiking across five continents, with Asia-Pacific currently meaning Japan, New Zealand and Thailand. This page is about the region that is missing, written for someone who will want the operational detail rather than the brochure.

facts.label: Asia-Pacific destinations on your map today
Where Ladakh starts, before any climbing
The band our Zanskar riding works in
The window, once the passes clear

angle.eyebrow: — The thing a Director of Product will notice first
angle.heading: Your activity levels measure climbing. The Himalaya measures altitude, which is a different axis entirely.
angle.body: Your scale runs one to four and measures the day: Level 4 road is 40–70 miles and up to 8,000 feet of climbing, Level 4 gravel 30–50 miles and up to 4,000. Ladakh does not sit anywhere on it. It starts at 11,500 feet of elevation before a wheel turns and rides between 11,500 and 17,700, where the limit is acclimatization rather than watts — a Level 2 day at 16,000 feet asks more of a guest than a Level 4 at home. Whatever you build here needs altitude as a second axis beside climbing, and we would rather raise that across a table than let you find it on a recce.

cards.title: Gravel
cards.body: Your only off-road line, and the one that fits. Past the sealed highways Ladakh is jeep track, caravan route and village road — Checkpoint terrain, point-to-point between villages, with almost no traffic because there is almost nobody. Worth saying plainly: the program we run in Zanskar today is shuttle-supported singletrack, which is not a style you sell. The gravel is the part that maps.
cards.note: Card retitled 15 Sep: it read 'Gravel and Cross Country'. Trek Travel's Cross Country is the coast-to-coast USA road trip, not MTB cross-country, and they run no singletrack product at all — their off-road line is Gravel on the Checkpoint. Confirm we can actually build a gravel week in Ladakh off unpaved road rather than trail.

cards.title: Hiking & Walking
cards.body: The same valleys work on foot, which means one region can carry two of your product lines rather than one.

specifics.title: Trek is not a new name to us.
specifics.body: The Adventure Provision Company, our authorized Trek retailer in Shreveport, Louisiana, is where our own bike knowledge comes from. Your fleet is a platform we already know rather than a spec sheet we would be reading for the first time — the Checkpoint you put people on for gravel included.

specifics.title: Shuttle-supported, with our own rig and crew.
specifics.body: Below Khar Kongma at Zangla, a short cliffy descent becomes repeatable laps. Five seasons of our own crews in Ladakh and twenty-plus across the Himalaya — the drop-ins and the viewpoints have been refined rather than scouted.

specifics.title: The soft start is not optional.
specifics.body: Two low days at Nimmu House, a heritage home where the Indus and Zanskar meet, before anyone rides. Skipping it is how a strong group has a bad week.

specifics.title: Season is the hard constraint.
specifics.body: Late April to early October, when the passes clear and the ground is firm. Outside it the valleys are shut — no negotiating.

specifics.title: And the road question, which is yours to answer.
specifics.body: Trek Travel is a road company first, and Ladakh's sealed passes are a road proposition almost nobody sells: Taglang La at 17,480 feet on the Manali–Leh highway, Khardung La at 17,582, and Umling La at 19,024 — the highest paved road on earth, in permit-controlled border country. Whether that becomes a trip depends on what we can support, which is the question to put to us in the room.

closing.heading: A region nobody in your category sells.
closing.body: If it is worth a recce, that is the ask. Twelve minutes is enough to decide whether it goes on a list for next year.

specificsNote: CORRECTED 15 Sep after checking Trek Travel's own site. (1) The card titled 'Gravel and Cross Country' conflated their Cross Country USA road trip with MTB cross-country; Trek Travel sells no singletrack product, so the card is now Gravel alone and says outright that our Zanskar program is not a style they sell. (2) The activity-level line cited only the road ceiling (8,000 ft) while pitching off-road; it now carries the gravel ceiling (4,000 ft) too, and the scale is four levels, not five. (3) Tenure made concrete at Will's direction: 5+ years in Ladakh, 20+ across the Himalaya — not 20 in Ladakh. (4) A fourth specific adds the sealed high passes, framed as an open question, because a road-first operator should hear that Umling La exists. VERIFIED and correct as written: three Asia-Pacific destinations (Japan, New Zealand, Thailand); Level 4 road 40–70 mi / up to 8,000 ft; Level 4 gravel 30–50 mi / up to 4,000 ft; Hiking & Walking is a real trip style. Pass heights are GPS-measured, never the Khardung La signboard's 18,379 ft. ADDED 15 Sep at Will's direction: The Adventure Provision Company (3787 Youree Dr, Shreveport LA; Trek lists it as a Preferred retailer, and it carries Trek road, mountain and Electra plus Yeti). Will asked to keep this to FAMILIARITY ONLY — no mechanics, no service department, no spares or support claims, which we cannot make in Ladakh anyway. CHECK THE WORDING: the page says 'our authorized Trek retailer', which reads as affiliation. Will did not state the corporate relationship; soften to 'a Trek retailer we work with' if that is wrong.

name: Javi Galvez
title: CEO
headline: Good to meet you,
Javi
lede: A Spanish company operating exclusively in the Nordics, meeting an American-led company operating exclusively in the Himalaya. Neither of us is buying anything today, which makes this one of the more interesting twelve minutes of the week.

facts.label: Nordic countries you operate in
Himalayan countries we operate in
Overlap in the map
Ground operations, both of us

angle.eyebrow: — Two operators of extreme terrain, opposite ends of the earth
angle.heading: You run volcanoes and glaciers. We run 16,400-foot passes. The operational problems are almost identical.
angle.body: Weather windows that close without warning, permits and access rights, guests who under-estimate the environment, and no supplier chain to fall back on. Companies that do this are rare enough that comparing notes is worth more than a referral agreement — though the referral is easy too.

cards.title: Referral, both directions
cards.body: Your guest who has done Greenland and wants altitude, ours who has done Zanskar and wants ice. Neither of us loses anything by sending them.

cards.title: How you handle the hard parts
cards.body: Guest screening for extreme terrain, insurance, evacuation, and how you price a trip whose season might not open. We would genuinely like to know how you do it.

specifics.title: Glaciers, from the other side.
specifics.body: Ours are at 16,400 feet and retreating fast enough that route notes go out of date between seasons. Yours are at sea level. The measurement problems are probably the same.

specifics.title: Adrenaline product, without a safety net.
specifics.body: You run extreme tours; so do we. In Zanskar the nearest hospital is a day's drive, which changes what you are willing to sell.

specifics.title: Small operators, own crews.
specifics.body: Neither of us subcontracts. That is the whole reason either of us can promise anything.

closing.heading: No pitch.
closing.body: Eleanor's read was that a Nordic specialist and a Himalayan one have no natural commercial fit, and that is right. Peer conversation and a standing referral is the honest ceiling, and it is worth having.
